steps.body: Picking the right unit makes numbers sensible. A book measured in inches gives a friendly number like 9; measured in feet it would be an awkward fraction. Small objects: inches. Big spaces: feet.

widget.prompt: Which unit is best to measure the length of a book?

options.label: inches
options.feedback: Yes — a book is small, so inches give a sensible number.

options.label: feet
options.feedback: Feet are for bigger things. A book is better measured in inches.

explanationVariants: A classroom is large, so feet fit best.

widget.prompt: Which unit is best to measure the length of a classroom?

options.label: feet
options.feedback: Yes — a classroom is large, so feet are the right size unit.

options.label: inches
options.feedback: Inches are for small things, like a book. A classroom is better measured in feet.

steps.body: Once you've chosen the unit and lined up the ruler, reading the length is the same subtraction every time: end mark minus start mark.

widget.prompt: A hand starts at 0 and ends at the mark labeled 7 on an inch ruler. How long is it?

commonPlacements.feedback: 0 is where it starts, not its length. It ends at 7, so it's 7.
Read the end mark itself, not one past it. The length is 7.

widget.successFeedback: It ends at 7, starting from 0, so it's 7 inches.
widget.alignFeedback: Align zero with the object's starting mark at 0 before counting units.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: Cover only the distance from 0 to 7 with equal units — no gaps, overlaps, or extra units.
widget.unitFeedback: Use one-inch units so the unit count is the length in inches.

steps.body: A car is much bigger than a book or a hand — a completely different scale calls for the bigger unit, feet.

widget.prompt: Which unit is best to measure the length of a car?

options.label: feet
options.feedback: Yes — a car is large, so feet are the right size unit.

options.label: inches
options.feedback: Inches would give a huge, awkward number for something as big as a car. Use feet.

explanationVariants: Subtract the start from the end: 6.

widget.prompt: A book starts at 3 and ends at 9 on an inch ruler. How long is it?

commonErrors.feedback: 9 is just the end mark. Subtract the start: 9 − 3 = 6.

explanationVariants: A hand is small, so inches fit best.
For very small objects, use inches.

widget.prompt: Which unit is best to measure the length of a hand?

options.label: inches
options.feedback: Yes — a hand is small, so inches are the right size unit.

options.label: feet
options.feedback: Feet are for bigger things. A hand is better measured in inches.

explanationVariants: Subtract the start from the end: 6.

widget.prompt: A crayon starts at 4 and ends at 10 on an inch ruler. How long is it?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 is just the end mark. Subtract the start: 10 − 4 = 6.

hints: Length is end mark minus start mark.

steps.body: Choose the unit that fits the size, then measure by subtracting start from end.
takeaways: Small objects: inches. Big spaces: feet.
The right unit gives friendly, sensible numbers.
Reading a ruler is always end mark minus start mark.
